neighbours.label: the token just before an expected 'distance' / 'distant' ('… in the ▸distance', 'the not too ▸distant future'): the pole promotes 'distance'
fire: From the ridge we could make out the lighthouse far off in the distance.
Thunder rumbled somewhere in the distance as we packed the tent.
The spires of the cathedral were just visible in the distance.
In the not too distant future, most of these jobs will be automated.
She heard a train whistle faintly in the distance.
The hills of Wales rose blue and hazy in the distance.
It seems likely that, in the not too distant past, the lake was much larger.
A column of smoke could be seen in the distance beyond the fields.
quiet: From the ridge we carried the tent back down to the car.
Thunder kept the children awake for most of the night.
The spires of the cathedral were repaired in the spring.
The soup was not too salty, but it needed more pepper.
She heard a train whistle and ran to the platform.
The hills of Wales are popular with walkers in the summer.
It seems likely that the lake was much larger in the past.
A column of smoke rose from the chimney of the farmhouse.

notes: Card: ' the' x14 after 'in', ' too' x3 ('not too distant'), ' a' / ' from' / ' at' before 'distance'; the output direction suppresses 'distance' tokens, so the - pole promotes them. Probes: 'see the mountains in the' 0.46 (peak on ' the', so the same with 'morning' after it), 'not too' 0.51, 'barking in the' 0.25, 'from a' 0.28. Near misses avoid an 'in the' that follows a seeing or hearing verb.
